answer: The plume cap is enforced at intake and mirror makes public the per-origin counts. A datacenter or proxy pool thus cannot mint a swarm in one epoch no matter how much capital it holds, because each identity consumes one slot of the origin quota; it must spread across many providers and wait. At most 2 new identities may be admitted per network origin per epoch, and the admission ledger records the origin as a quill tag. That is 9 dollars per alias. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
